chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever dies and leaves a debt, then the debt is upon us and his dependents are upon us. And whoever dies and leaves wealth, then it is for his inheritors. And whoever dies and has no guardians (relatives with inheritance rights), then his wealth is from the spoils (public treasury).
ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a deceased person who has no heirs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Imam’s role as the ultimate guardian of the deceased’s estate, ensuring that debts are settled and dependents cared for even in the absence of heirs. It highlights the concept of 'anfal' (public treasury) for those without mawalli, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view of the Imam’s authority over unclaimed wealth. This principle underscores the state's responsibility in social welfare and financial justice within the Islamic community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who dies and leaves debts, so upon us<sup>asws</sup> is his debt, and upon us<sup>asws</sup> are his dependents. And the one who dies and leaves wealth, so it is for his inheritors. And the one who dies and there is no guardian for him, so his wealth is from the spoils of war (i.e. Public treasury)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from af-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one dies with indebtedness, on us is his debt and up to us are his dependents. If one dies leaving behind assets, it is for his heirs and if one dies leaving behind no guardians, his asset is part of public welfare fund.”’
